does: Mixes soft cheese with well-squeezed greens, grated hard cheese and egg into a thick, even filling that holds its shape and sets lightly in the oven.

intro.what: Soft cheese, drained greens, hard cheese and egg are mixed into a filling that holds together.
intro.why: A filling that is too wet runs out of the pasta and makes the dish watery. Squeezing the greens and binding with egg keep it firm.

how: Squeeze the cooked greens hard so that no more water runs from them, and chop them fine.
Drain any liquid from the soft cheese.
Mix the cheese, the greens, the grated hard cheese and the egg with the seasoning until evenly coloured.
Taste and season before the egg goes in, then mix it in.

cues.text: The filling holds its shape on a spoon and does not run.
It is one even colour with no streaks of white cheese.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving water in the greens, so that the filling runs and the dish is watery.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the greens hard by the handful.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving out the egg, so that the filling falls out when it is cut.
mistakes.fix: Bind it with egg, which sets in the oven.

quiz.question: Why is the filling bound with egg?
choices: So that it sets in the oven and holds together.
quiz.because: The egg sets with heat and binds the filling.

quiz.question: What must be done to the greens first?
choices: Squeeze them hard and chop them.
quiz.because: Water left in the greens makes the filling runny.

quiz.question: How should a good filling behave on a spoon?
choices: It holds its shape and is one colour.
quiz.because: A thick, even filling stays in the pasta.

quiz.question: The baked dish was watery and the filling ran. What would you change next time?
choices: Squeeze the greens harder and drain the cheese.
quiz.because: Water from the greens and the cheese is the cause.

comes_after.why: The greens are squeezed dry before they go into the filling.
